title: Definition of Probability Measure
text:
2. Definition
Let \((\Omega, \mathcal{F})\) be a measurable space. A set function \(P: \mathcal{F} \to [0, 1]\) is called a probability measure if it satisfies the following conditions:

\(P(\Omega) = 1\).
(Countable Additivity) For any pairwise disjoint sequence of events \(\{E_n\}_{n=1}^\infty \subset \mathcal{F}\), \[
P\left( \bigcup_{n=1}^\infty E_n \right) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty P(E_n)
\]

title: Definition of Probability Measure
text:
3. Example
If we consider a fair coin toss, \(\Omega = \{H, T\}\) and \(P(\{H\}) = P(\{T\}) = 0.5\).
